detailed_rationale:
KPI Green Energy is a Gujarat-based renewable energy developer running a dual EPC-to-IPP model: it builds solar and wind-solar hybrid capacity, retaining some as an Independent Power Producer (IPP, annuity-style long-term PPA revenue) and building-operating-transferring the rest to Captive Power Producer (CPP) clients who are also equity holders in the underlying SPV, which de-risks the offtake. FY26 (year to Mar 2026) revenue came in at roughly Rs 2,696 crore with PAT of about Rs 476 crore, and Q1 FY26 (June 2025) net profit was up 68% YoY to Rs 111.32 crore on revenue of Rs 614 crore (+75% YoY) -- consistent with the 55-61% top-line growth the quant screen captures (revenue_cagr_3y 61.2%, revenue_growth_1y 55.4%). The company has scaled fast: cumulative installed plus upcoming capacity is now about 4.74 GW (2.17 GW IPP, 2.57 GW CPP), with a 376 MW GUVNL IPP project at Khavda commissioned in January 2026 and 250 MW / 370 MW projects targeted for commercial operations by October 2026, plus 150 MW of wind by November 2027. The order book is large -- 3.61 GW plus a separate CPP order book of about Rs 5,246 crore -- implying multi-year revenue visibility if executed on schedule.

Three quality-of-earnings issues sit underneath the growth headline, however. First, margin composition: IPP-segment EBITDA margins are reported at 85-90%, but consolidated Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin was only about 38% -- meaning the bulk of current revenue is still lower-margin, lumpy EPC/CPP construction revenue rather than mature annuity IPP cashflow, so the growth rate is partly a build-out artifact rather than a steady-state generation business yet. Second, execution has not been flawless: the flagship Khavda IPP project faced power-evacuation delays against the company's own January/September 2025 timelines, and labour issues were reported at the site in September 2025. Third, governance signals are mixed: promoters have pledged 44.7% of their holding, promoter stake has drifted down about 5.3 percentage points over three years, the board approved a Rs 475 crore warrant issue to promoter entity Quoyosh Energia at Rs 470.30/warrant (about 4.87% dilution on full conversion), and related-party transactions for project development totalled Rs 68.75 crore. None of these individually disqualify the story, but together they help explain why the stock has fallen 21.8% over one year and 33.3% over two years even as reported growth has stayed strong -- the market is discounting execution, dilution and governance risk against the headline CAGR. Balance sheet metrics remain serviceable (D/E 1.71x, interest coverage 5.3x) rather than distressed, and the quant screen scores quality and growth very highly (quality_score 83.3, growth_3y_score 96.3, growth_1y_score 93.8) while value_score is only middling (47.1) and price momentum is clearly negative.
recommendation_rationale: The quant screen already carries this as Hold (strong quality/growth scores offset by a middling value score and weak price momentum). My own read agrees: growth is real and the pipeline is large, but the current ~16.9x trailing PE is not obviously cheap once adjusted for (a) EPC/CPP revenue still being lower-quality than mature annuity IPP cashflow, (b) a fresh equity/warrant issue diluting existing holders to help fund the buildout, and (c) demonstrated execution slippage on the flagship Khavda project. There is no clean basis to rescue this to a stronger call, nor is there a genuine analytical tension that rises to the escalation bar -- the risks here (pledge, dilution, delays) are already visible in public filings and are already showing up in the two-year price decline, which is exactly the ordinary-uncertainty case the skill says not to escalate. Hold is the right call: don't chase the growth story, but the underlying business is not distressed either.
summary: KPI Green Energy is a fast-growing Gujarat renewable-power developer (solar and wind, IPP plus captive-power models) that has compounded revenue at 55%+ over the past year on an expanding roughly 4.7 GW capacity base and a large project pipeline (3.61 GW order book). But margins today are still driven mostly by lower-quality EPC/construction revenue rather than mature annuity power generation, the flagship Khavda project has seen commissioning delays, and the promoter has both pledged a large share of holdings and diluted existing shareholders via a fresh warrant issue to fund growth. We rate it a Hold: the growth pipeline is genuine, but at this valuation the execution and governance risks are not yet fully proven out, so this is one to watch rather than add to.
positive_para: A genuine multi-year growth runway -- a 3.61 GW order book plus a roughly Rs 5,246 crore CPP order book against a current operating base of well under 1 GW -- with a shift already underway toward higher-margin annuity IPP capacity (85-90% segment EBITDA margins) away from EPC/CPP construction revenue. The CPP model itself is de-risked because the offtaker is also an equity holder in the underlying project SPV, and at roughly 16.9x trailing earnings the stock is not priced for perfection relative to the growth already delivered, accounting-quality caveats aside.
negative_para: The headline growth is still substantially EPC/construction-revenue-driven -- consolidated Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin of about 38% is far below the 85-90% margin quoted for the IPP segment, meaning today's PAT quality is not yet representative of the mature, contracted-cashflow business the bull case underwrites. Execution has already slipped once (Khavda evacuation delays versus the company's own 2025 guidance, plus reported labour issues at the site), promoters have pledged 44.7% of their stake and diluted shareholders via a Rs 475 crore warrant issue to a promoter-linked entity, and the stock's own price action (-21.8% over one year, -33.3% over two years) shows the market already marking this down -- a name to watch for proof of execution, not to average into blind.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At about 16.9x trailing earnings, the market is not pricing hypergrowth-forever -- it implies roughly high-teens/low-20s% sustained earnings growth with some margin normalization, which is achievable if the 3.61 GW pipeline converts on schedule and the IPP mix keeps rising. But the multiple already reflects a risk discount from the Khavda delays and the dilution, so this reads as fair-to-cheap on growth alone rather than clearly cheap once quality-of-earnings and dilution are priced in. Growth here is estimated below the 25% hypergrowth band, so the ROE/dilution disclosure is not separately mandated by the rules, but it is worth noting anyway: ROE is 23.1% (respectable), yet the just-approved roughly 4.87% warrant dilution to a promoter entity shows this growth is not being fully self-funded from internal accruals.
